name: Mesopotamian and Egyptian Civilizations

objectives.text: Identify Egypt as a land along the Nile River where Joseph and Moses lived
Name Ur of the Chaldeans as Abraham's first home and retell how God called him to leave it
Describe how people in Abraham's world built cities and towers out of baked mud bricks
Describe what a Mesopotamian ziggurat looked like and explain how the tower of Babel account reflects this kind of building
Locate the Fertile Crescent, the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, and the Nile River on a map
Explain how the yearly flooding of the Nile supplied Egypt with food and why famine sent Jacob's family to Egypt
Compare the life of an Israelite shepherd with the life of an Egyptian city dweller using details from the Joseph narrative
Identify Egyptian court customs in the Joseph narrative such as the signet ring, linen garments, chariots, and Egyptian names
Locate Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, and Persia on a Bible map and explain why Israel's location placed it between these powers
Describe the role of Pharaoh as a king regarded as divine and explain how Exodus presents the conflict between Pharaoh and the LORD
Describe Egyptian forced labor and royal building projects as background to Israel's bondage
Analyze the struggle between the northern empires of Assyria and Babylon and the southern power of Egypt and how Judah's kings were pulled between them
Explain how the plagues of Egypt are presented as the LORD's judgment on the gods of Egypt
Explain the Assyrian policy of deporting and resettling conquered peoples and how it shaped the fall of Samaria
Explain how Babylon deported and retrained the leading people of Judah as background to the book of Daniel
Analyze Sennacherib's campaign against Judah by comparing the biblical account with Assyrian royal records
Analyze how the prophets describe Assyria and Babylon as instruments in God's hand who are still accountable for their pride and cruelty
Evaluate the archaeological and textual evidence bearing on Israel's sojourn in Egypt
Evaluate how Mesopotamian records such as the Babylonian Chronicles, the Jehoiachin ration tablets, and the Cyrus Cylinder relate to the biblical accounts
Construct an account of the rise and fall of the ancient Near Eastern empires that connects them to the Reformed reading of God's sovereignty in Daniel's visions

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (Egypt and the Nile, Ur, ziggurats, Fertile Crescent, Nile agriculture, shepherd versus city life, map work, northern and southern empires, plagues and Egyptian gods, Assyrian warfare, evidence for Israel in Egypt, Daniel and the empires). Dropped the clay writing objective as belonging to Languages, the Code of Hammurabi as belonging to Law Codes, and the vague cradle of civilization item. Replaced the defend reliability objective with a specific evaluation of named Mesopotamian records. Added objectives on Joseph's Egyptian court setting, Pharaoh's divine kingship, Egyptian forced labor, Assyrian deportation, Babylonian exile practice, Sennacherib's campaign, and the prophets' view of empires under God's providence, with scripture and confession anchors where they apply.
